as explained in the linked explanatory memorandum
For liable departures from 1 January 2027, this bill would raise the passenger movement charge to $80 instead of $70.
Passengers whose tickets were sold on or before Royal Assent would retain the $70 rate for departures through 30 June 2028.
From 1 July 2028, liable departures would attract the $80 rate regardless of when the ticket was bought.
Raises the charge on eligible departures from Australia by $10.
Ties the new rate to departure dates from January 2027, with an eighteen-month transition for qualifying earlier bookings.
Keeps the existing rate during that transition for tickets or equivalent travel authorities issued before commencement.
Ends the earlier-booking exception for departures from July 2028.
Travellers liable for the charge, airlines, shipping and charter operators, and border officials collecting it are affected.

Moved the second reading of a bill increasing the passenger movement charge from $70 to $80 from 1 January 2027 and aligning its calculation with the departure date. The bill would provide an 18-month carrier transition period and increase revenue by $755 million over four years from 2026-27 to 2029-30.

Declared that the Combatting Illicit Tobacco Bill 2026, the Australia's Foreign Relations (State and Territory Arrangements) Amendment Bill 2026, the Counter-Terrorism Legislation Amendment Bill 2026 and the Passenger Movement Charge Amendment Bill 2026 stand referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.
